subject: science
title: Light
description: That we need light to see, how light reflects from surfaces, protecting eyes from the Sun, and how shadows are formed and change.

objectives.statement: Recognise that they need light in order to see things and that dark is the absence of light.
Notice that light is reflected from surfaces.
Recognise that light from the sun can be dangerous and that there are ways to protect their eyes.
Recognise that shadows are formed when the light from a light source is blocked by an opaque object.
Find patterns in the way that the size of shadows change.

items.prompt: What do we need in order to see things?

items.statement: Dark is simply the absence of light.

items.prompt: In a room with no light at all, how well can you see the objects around you?
Which of these is a source of light?

items.statement: A cat can see in a room that has absolutely no light at all.

items.prompt: What happens to light when it hits a mirror?
Which surface reflects light the best?

items.statement: Shiny, smooth surfaces reflect light better than dull, rough ones.

items.prompt: Why do cyclists wear reflective strips at night?
options: so light from car headlights bounces back and drivers can see them

items.statement: A mirror makes its own light.
It is safe to look straight at the Sun for a long time.

items.prompt: Name one way you can protect your eyes from the Sun.
items.answer: Wear sunglasses or a sun hat, and never look straight at the Sun

items.prompt: Which of these helps protect your eyes on a very bright, sunny day?

items.statement: Light from the Sun can damage your eyes.

items.answer: An opaque object blocks light from a light source

items.prompt: Which kind of object makes the darkest shadow?
options: an opaque object that blocks all light

items.statement: A shadow forms on the same side as the light source.

items.prompt: What happens to an object's shadow as you move the light source closer to it?

items.statement: Moving an object further from a light source can change the size of its shadow.

items.prompt: Why does a shadow have roughly the same shape as the object that makes it?
items.answer: Because the object blocks the light in that shape
acceptableAnswers: the object blocks the light in its shape
the light is blocked in the shape of the object
